phases.title: Plan the prompt
phases.route: Warehousing ➔ Inventory Reporting ➔ Inventory Position ➔ Company - Item Inventory

tokens.v: A prompt is tied to one exact session code, and its dataset to that session's table. From that table a dataset reaches the tables it points to and the tables that point at it, and nothing beyond. So the build starts with what the answer must say, and then finds the screen whose record owns that data. The example's stock rows belong to an item's warehousing record, which is what Company - Item Inventory lists. LN has no language model of its own: it keeps a list retrieved from the Infor GenAI application, and a prompt that names no model uses the one that service marks as default.

phases.title: Model the dataset
phases.route: Tools ➔ Application Extensibility ➔ Embedded GenAI ➔ Datasets

tokens.v: A dataset is the LN data that travels with the question, and it is the whole of what the model is told. It starts from one main table and one index of it. The record the user is on reaches the dataset through that index, which is why both have to be the screen's own. Around the main table the Modeler offers two branches: Refers to, for a value behind a code, and Referred by, for rows that belong to the record. Every field ticked is sent, so take only what the prompt text will name.

tokens.v: A prompt row ties a label, a dataset and two texts together. The label's description becomes the command's name. The instruction text is shown to the user beside the answer. The prompt text is what is sent to the model, with the dataset's output put where its data marker stands. The first prompt text is short on purpose: what the data is, the task, one rule and the marker.

tokens.v: When the command is chosen, LN runs the dataset for the record on the screen, writes the result into the prompt text and sends it to the model. The answer opens in a window of its own. The model answers only from what the dataset sent, and a wrong answer looks the same as a right one, so the first run is checked against the screen and then read for what nobody asked for.
